evidence: Full CDIAL *māḍa upper storey includes Prakrit māla upper part of a house, Gujarati māḷ loft/upper storey, māḷɔ loft/large house and specifically māḷiyũ loft; Marathi māḷā loft supplies a further regional lateral form. Survey māḷya/māḷiyā/maḷai/malu roof fit this upper-part-of-house family with retained vowel and ending variation. Roof versus loft is a qualified semantic identification, and local IA transmission remains unresolved. The remote Dravidian origin printed in the article is not an assertion of direct Dravidian borrowing by the survey languages. Search-linked māla 10088 instead means forest/garden and was rejected as evidence.
